day_by_day.morning: Arrival day — no morning activities scheduled. Flight LH lands at 13:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing and clearing customs, take the Leonardo Express train from Fiumicino Airport to Roma Termini (€14), then connect via Metro Line A to Ottaviano station, a short walk to your hotel in the Borgo district. Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation stroll through the charming Borgo Pio pedestrian street and the medieval alleyways surrounding your accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the iconic Castel Sant'Angelo for a stunning free exterior view at sunset along the Tiber River. Explore the nearby Piazza Navona (free entry) to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers and soak in the lively atmosphere of street artists and locals.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick coffee and cornetto at the airport or on arrival — skip or keep it light.
meals.lunch: Pick up a supplì (fried rice ball) and a slice of pizza al taglio from a local bakery near Termini or in the Borgo area for around €4–6.
meals.dinner: Trattoria Pizzarium-style meal at a local neighbourhood spot near Borgo Pio — try Osteria dell'Angelo or a similar family-run trattoria with a fixed-price menu (menù del giorno) for €10–15 including pasta and house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Keep luggage minimal while sightseeing. Validate all public transport tickets before boarding to avoid fines.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early (by 7:30 AM) and head to the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel. Book tickets online in advance (€17 standard entry) to skip the long queues. Spend 2–3 hours marvelling at the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling — one of the world's greatest art experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exit through St. Peter's Basilica (free entry — just a short walk from the museum exit). Climb to the top of St. Peter's Dome for panoramic views of Rome (€8 with elevator, €6 on foot). Spend time in St. Peter's Square and the Basilica interior, which is completely free and filled with masterpieces including Michelangelo's Pietà.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll across the beautiful Ponte Sant'Angelo bridge and walk along the Tiber embankment. Head to the lively Trastevere neighbourhood (20-minute walk or short bus ride) for an evening of wandering through cobblestone streets, browsing street art, and enjoying the vibrant local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Bar San Pietro or any local café near the hotel — espresso and cornetto for €1.50–2.50. The classic Roman breakfast.
meals.lunch: Grab a panino or pizza al taglio near the Vatican — try I Supplì Roma or any alimentari (deli) near Via della Conciliazione for €5–8.
meals.dinner: Trastevere is perfect for budget dining. Try Da Enzo al 29 or Tonnarello for hearty Roman pasta dishes like cacio e pepe or amatriciana for €10–14 per person including a glass of house wine.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums are extremely popular — booking online is essential, especially in June. Dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees) for entry into the Basilica and Museums. Arrive at the Museums right at opening time for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Take Metro Line A from Ottaviano to Spagna station and visit the Spanish Steps (free) early in the morning before crowds gather. Walk through the elegant Via Condotti window-shopping area, then head to the stunning Trevi Fountain (free) — toss a coin for good luck. Explore the surrounding Baroque streets of the historic centre.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Pantheon (€5 entry — one of the best-preserved ancient buildings in the world, free for under 18s). Admire the 2,000-year-old unreinforced concrete dome and the oculus that lets in natural light. Nearby, explore the charming Piazza della Rotonda and surrounding lanes. Then walk to Campo de' Fiori for a browse of the afternoon market stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Ghetto neighbourhood (free walking) — one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric districts. Walk along the ancient Portico d'Ottavia ruins at dusk. Return to the hotel via a scenic walk along the Tiber or take Bus 23.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel or grab a quick espresso standing at the bar — €1–2.
meals.lunch: Eat near the Pantheon at Forno del Ghetto or grab a classic Roman sandwich from a nearby alimentari. Budget €6–9. Avoid the tourist traps immediately surrounding the Pantheon.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal using ingredients from Campo de' Fiori market, or dine at a local pizzeria near the Borgo district — Pizzarium (by Bonci) near the Vatican is legendary for gourmet pizza al taglio at €5–10.

day_by_day.notes: June mornings at the Trevi Fountain are still crowded by 9 AM — aim to arrive before 8:30 AM for the best photos. Many churches along this route (Sant'Ignazio, Santa Maria sopra Minerva) are free to enter and contain extraordinary art.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill — book the combined ticket online in advance (€16 for all three sites). Spend the morning exploring the iconic Colosseum interior, imagining gladiatorial contests. Allow 1.5–2 hours inside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Use your combined ticket to walk through the Roman Forum and up to Palatine Hill — the birthplace of Rome. These sites are included in the same ticket and take 2–3 hours to explore properly. The views over the Forum from Palatine Hill are spectacular. Nearby, the Circus Maximus is free to view from outside.
day_by_day.evening: Walk up Aventine Hill (free) to the famous Knights of Malta keyhole on Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta — peer through for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome. Nearby, the Orange Garden (Giardino degli Aranci) offers one of Rome's best free panoramic viewpoints at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Café near your hotel — espresso and pastry for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a nearby alimentari or supermarket (Conad or Carrefour Express) before heading out — bread, cheese, prosciutto, and fruit for €5–7. Eat in the shade near the Circus Maximus.
meals.dinner: Try Testaccio neighbourhood, Rome's true food district. Visit Flavio al Velavevodetto or a local trattoria for offal-free Roman classics like rigatoni alla carbonara or coda alla vaccinara for €12–16.

day_by_day.notes: June heat can be intense at the Colosseum and Forum — bring water, sunscreen, and a hat. The sites are very exposed with little shade. Start as early as possible (9 AM opening). The combined ticket is valid for 24 hours across all three sites.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery — one of Rome's finest art museums housing Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio paintings. Advance booking is mandatory (€15 entry, timed entry every 2 hours). Located in the beautiful Villa Borghese park, arrive early and enjoy the gardens before your entry time. The gallery limits visitors, making it an intimate and extraordinary art experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, explore the vast Villa Borghese park for free — rent a rowboat on the lake (€3–5), stroll through gardens, and visit the free Pincian Hill terrace for sweeping views over Rome and Piazza del Popolo below. Walk down to Piazza del Popolo (free) and admire the twin Baroque churches and ancient Egyptian obelisk.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Prati neighbourhood near your hotel — Rome's upscale but accessible residential area with excellent local restaurants, gelaterias, and bars. Browse Via Cola di Rienzo for local shopping and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Bar near the hotel — try a maritozzo (cream-filled bun, a Roman classic) with cappuccino for €3–4.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese park — pick up supplies from a nearby supermarket or deli for €6–8. Eating in the park is a quintessential Roman experience.
meals.dinner: Dine in Prati neighbourhood — try Osteria dell'Angelo (authentic Roman trattoria, cash only, fixed menu around €15) or explore the many affordable pizza and pasta restaurants along Via Candia.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets sell out weeks in advance in June — book as early as possible online at the official website. The gallery only allows 360 visitors at a time, making it one of Rome's most peaceful and rewarding art experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the lesser-known but spectacular Palazzo Altemps (€10, or €12 combined with other national museums) near Piazza Navona — a Renaissance palace housing ancient Roman sculpture including the famous Ludovisi Throne. Far fewer crowds than major sites. Afterward, explore the beautiful Sant'Agostino church (free) which contains a Caravaggio painting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take Bus 40 or 64 to visit the stunning Basilica di San Giovanni in Laterano (free entry) — Rome's cathedral and one of the four major basilicas. Nearby, the Scala Santa (Holy Staircase) and the ancient Baptistery are free to visit. Walk to the Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore (free) for more extraordinary free art and architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere for a final evening exploration — visit the beautiful Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free, stunning 12th-century mosaics), enjoy an Aperol Spritz at a local bar (€4–6), and browse the evening street market atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Local café near hotel — espresso and cornetto for €2.
meals.lunch: Near San Giovanni — try a local trattoria or rosticceria (roast chicken shop) for a filling lunch for €7–10. The neighbourhood around San Giovanni is very local and affordable.
meals.dinner: Trastevere farewell dinner — splurge slightly at a well-reviewed local restaurant. Try pasta e ceci (pasta with chickpeas) or a classic Roman artichoke dish (carciofi alla romana) for €12–16. End with artisan gelato from Fatamorgana for €3–4.

day_by_day.notes: The combination of lesser-visited churches and museums today offers world-class art without the crowds or high entry fees. Carry a small flashlight or use your phone torch inside darker basilicas to better appreciate the mosaics and artwork.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — revisit your favourite spot for a peaceful early morning experience (the Trevi Fountain before 8 AM, St. Peter's Square at sunrise, or a quiet walk along the Tiber). Visit the nearby free Castel Sant'Angelo interior if you haven't yet (€15) for rooftop views and fascinating history as a papal fortress and mausoleum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Mercato Trionfale (Rome's largest covered food market, near Via Andrea Doria — 10-minute walk from hotel) — open until early afternoon on weekdays. Browse local produce, cheeses, cured meats, and street food. Pick up edible souvenirs like dried pasta, truffle products, or local olive oil at market prices rather than tourist shop prices.
day_by_day.evening: Depending on departure time — enjoy a final aperitivo hour (5–7 PM) in Prati with a Spritz or Negroni and free bar snacks (cicchetti). Pack, settle the hotel bill, and arrange transport to the airport. Take Metro A to Termini and Leonardo Express back to Fiumicino (allow 1.5–2 hours before departure).

meals.breakfast: Final Roman breakfast at your favourite local bar — savour that last espresso standing at the counter like a true Roman for €1–1.50.
meals.lunch: Mercato Trionfale lunch — graze on market food: fresh mozzarella, supplì, cured meats, and seasonal fruit for €6–10. The ultimate budget Roman food experience.
meals.dinner: Light dinner before departure or at the airport — or enjoy an early dinner at a Prati trattoria before heading to catch your flight.

day_by_day.notes: Leave ample time for airport transport — allow at least 2 hours before your flight for the journey from central Rome to Fiumicino. The Leonardo Express runs every 15 minutes and takes 32 minutes to the airport (€14). Store luggage at your hotel until departure if checking out early.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Hotel Check-In — Flight lands at 13:00, so the morning slot is occupied by travel. Take the Leonardo Express train from Fiumicino Airport to Roma Termini, then connect to your hotel in the Vatican/Borgo district. Settle in, freshen up, and get oriented with a short stroll along Via della Conciliazione toward St. Peter's Square for a first glimpse of the basilica exterior (free, no ticket needed).
day_by_day.afternoon: Neighborhood Orientation Walk — Explore the charming Borgo district on foot. Wander through Borgo Pio, a pedestrian medieval lane lined with cafés and artisan shops, then walk across the iconic Ponte Sant'Angelo to admire the Tiber River views and the angel statues. Browse the Castel Sant'Angelo exterior and its riverside promenade — a perfect, low-key introduction to Rome after a long flight.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — Join the guided Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk. Wander cobblestone streets sampling supplì (fried rice balls), Roman-style artichokes, local pecorino, and regional wines. This lively neighborhood is easily reachable by a short tram or taxi ride and is ideal for a first Roman evening.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick espresso and cornetto at a bar near Fiumicino or Roma Termini upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Light bite near the hotel — try Pizzarium Bonci (Via della Meloria), famous for gourmet pizza al taglio, perfect for a quick mid-range lunch after check-in.
meals.dinner: Included as tastings on the Trastevere Food & Wine Walk; supplement with a sit-down finish at Tonnarello (Via della Paglia, Trastevere) for classic cacio e pepe — budget-friendly and beloved by locals.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk in advance. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Carry a water bottle as June in Rome can be warm (likely 28–32°C). Validate all public transport tickets before boarding.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — Start early with a pre-booked skip-the-line ticket (opening time: 9:00 AM). Spend 3–4 hours exploring the Raphael Rooms, the Gallery of Maps, the Gallery of Tapestries, and culminate in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling. This is one of the world's greatest art collections and deserves a full, unhurried morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Peter's Basilica & Dome Climb — After the Museums, walk directly into St. Peter's Basilica (free entry). Marvel at Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's towering baldachin. For stunning panoramic views over Rome, climb the dome (elevator partway + stairs to the top; mid-range fee). Spend the late afternoon relaxing in St. Peter's Square, just steps from your hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Castel Sant'Angelo Night Visit — The castle offers extended evening hours in summer. Explore the fortress that once served as a papal refuge, with incredible nighttime views of Rome from its terrace. Afterward, enjoy a leisurely dinner in the Prati neighborhood, just north of your hotel.

meals.breakfast: At your boutique hotel or at a nearby bar — espresso, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and a warm cornetto alla crema.
meals.lunch: Il Sorpasso (Via Properzio, Prati) — a stylish mid-range spot beloved by locals for its cicchetti (small bites), craft beer, and seasonal Roman dishes. Perfect between Vatican and afternoon sightseeing.
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo (Via G. Bettolo, Prati) — a classic Roman trattoria serving traditional dishes like rigatoni alla pajata and abbacchio. Fixed-price menu is excellent value. Reserve ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets MUST be pre-booked online — walk-up queues can be 2–3 hours. Dress code enforced: covered shoulders and knees required for the Basilica. Arrive at the Museums at least 15 minutes before your entry slot.

day_by_day.morning: Pasta & Gelato Making Class — Join a hands-on morning cooking class in a traditional Roman kitchen. Learn to make fresh pasta (cacio e pepe or carbonara) from scratch with a local chef, then craft authentic gelato. Classes typically run 10:00 AM–1:00 PM and include eating your creations. This is a highlight for food lovers and a wonderful cultural immersion.
day_by_day.afternoon: Campo de' Fiori & Jewish Ghetto Exploration — After your class, walk to the vibrant Campo de' Fiori market square (winding down by early afternoon but still atmospheric). Then stroll into Rome's ancient Jewish Ghetto to explore Portico d'Ottavia ruins, the Great Synagogue, and charming piazzas. Browse local bakeries for Jewish-Roman specialties like ricotta cheesecake and almond cookies.
day_by_day.evening: Piazza Navona & Pantheon by Night — As the heat of the day fades, visit the magnificent Pantheon (check evening ticket availability) and then linger at Piazza Navona to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers illuminated at night. Enjoy gelato from a quality gelateria and soak in the electric Roman evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Quick espresso and pastry at Bar San Calisto in Trastevere or a café near the cooking class location.
meals.lunch: Eat what you made in the cooking class — the meal is included as part of the experience!
meals.dinner: Ristorante Fortunato al Pantheon (Via del Pantheon) — a well-regarded mid-range restaurant near the Pantheon serving refined Roman classics. Alternatively, Da Francesco (Piazza del Fico) for great wood-fired pizza in a lively setting.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Pasta & Gelato Making Class at least 1 week in advance — popular classes fill up fast. Wear comfortable shoes for the afternoon walking tour. The Pantheon now charges a small admission fee; book online to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour — Take a taxi or bus to Villa Borghese for your pre-booked timed entry (mandatory; entry every 2 hours, max 2 hours inside). Marvel at Bernini's breathtaking sculptures — Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina — and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings. This intimate gallery is arguably Rome's most rewarding art experience per square meter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Villa Borghese Gardens & Spanish Steps — After the gallery, spend a relaxed afternoon strolling through the beautiful Villa Borghese park. Rent a rowboat on the small lake, enjoy the greenery, and then descend the Pincian Hill terrace for sweeping views over Piazza del Popolo. Walk down to the iconic Spanish Steps and browse the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.evening: Trevi Fountain & Aperitivo Hour — Visit the spectacular Trevi Fountain in the early evening when it's beautifully lit (it's always busy, but magical at dusk). Toss a coin for good luck. Then enjoy a classic Roman aperitivo — Aperol Spritz or Negroni with complimentary snacks — at a bar in the surrounding Trevi/Quirinale neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: At your hotel or a nearby Prati café before heading to the gallery.
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese gardens — pick up fresh bread, local cheeses, cured meats, and fruit from a Prati deli (Salumeria Roscioli has a branch, or try a local alimentari). Eat on the grass like a Roman.
meals.dinner: Colline Emiliane (Via degli Avignonesi, near Trevi) — a beloved mid-range trattoria specializing in Emilian pasta like tortellini in brodo and tagliatelle al ragù. Cash only; reserve ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets must be booked weeks in advance — this is non-negotiable. Entry is strictly timed and cannot be extended. Keep your booking confirmation on your phone. The gallery is closed Mondays.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Exploration — Head to the ancient heart of Rome with a combined ticket for the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill. Start at Palatine Hill for sweeping views over the Forum, then descend into the Forum itself — walk the Sacred Way, see the Temple of Saturn, the Arch of Titus, and imagine Julius Caesar's world. Deeply moving and historically rich.
day_by_day.afternoon: Colosseum — Use your combined ticket to enter the iconic Colosseum. Explore the arena floor (if booked) and multiple levels for dramatic views of the interior. Afterward, rest your feet at a nearby café in the Celio neighborhood, a quiet residential area with great local bars away from tourist traps.
day_by_day.evening: Testaccio Neighborhood Food Exploration — Take a short walk or bus to Testaccio, Rome's authentic working-class food district. Browse the famous Testaccio Market (closing by 2 PM but the neighborhood stays lively), visit the street food stalls, and settle in for dinner at one of the neighborhood's legendary trattorias specializing in traditional Roman offal-based cuisine or classic pasta.

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel before heading out early — aim to be at the Forum by 9:00 AM before the heat and crowds build.
meals.lunch: Café Caffe Circus or a simple trattoria near the Colosseum — avoid the overpriced tourist spots directly opposite; walk one block further for better value. Try supplì and a cold beer.
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto (Via di Monte Testaccio) — a Testaccio institution carved into an ancient Monte Testaccio hill, serving exceptional cacio e pepe, amatriciana, and coda alla vaccinara (oxtail). Mid-range and unmissable.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Colosseum tickets with timed entry — same-day tickets are rarely available. Consider adding the arena floor access for an extra fee. Wear a hat and sunscreen; the Forum offers little shade in June. Bring 1.5L of water.

day_by_day.morning: Trastevere Morning Market & Neighborhood Walk — Spend a relaxed Saturday morning at the Porta Portese flea market (open until 2 PM) for antiques, vintage finds, and local color. Then wander into the heart of Trastevere — visit the stunning Santa Maria in Trastevere basilica with its glittering 12th-century mosaics (free entry), and explore the neighborhood's artisan shops and ivy-covered lanes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Janiculum Hill & Botanical Garden — Climb (or take a bus) to the Janiculum Hill (Gianicolo) for the best panoramic view of Rome's rooftops and domes — arguably better than any other viewpoint in the city. Visit the nearby Orto Botanico (Botanical Garden) for a cool, shaded respite. A peaceful and underrated afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Aperitivo & Special Dinner — Celebrate your penultimate evening with a refined dinner. Return to the Prati or Borgo neighborhood near your hotel for a memorable meal at a slightly elevated mid-range restaurant, pairing a Roman antipasto spread with handmade pasta and a bottle of local Frascati or Cesanese wine.

meals.breakfast: Bar San Calisto (Piazza di San Calisto, Trastevere) — a legendary, no-frills local bar. Excellent espresso and cornetti at rock-bottom prices, beloved by Romans.
meals.lunch: Da Enzo al 29 (Via dei Vascellari, Trastevere) — one of Rome's most authentic and beloved small trattorias. Arrive early or expect a wait. Perfect cacio e pepe and seasonal Roman vegetable dishes.
meals.dinner: Il Sorpasso (Prati) for a relaxed aperitivo spread, or upgrade to Settimio all'Arancio (Via dell'Arancio) near Piazza Navona for a refined but mid-range Roman dinner with an excellent wine list.

day_by_day.notes: Porta Portese is busiest early — arrive by 8:30–9:00 AM for the best finds and before the crowds. Santa Maria in Trastevere is free but has a modest dress code. The Janiculum cannon fires at noon daily — a beloved Roman tradition.

day_by_day.morning: Slow Sunday Morning — Embrace the Roman Sunday pace. Attend Mass at St. Peter's Basilica (free, deeply atmospheric, especially if the Pope is present for the Angelus prayer at noon in the square) or simply enjoy a long, leisurely breakfast at a Prati café. Browse the weekly organic market at Circus Maximus if energy allows (open Sunday mornings).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last Museum or Hidden Gem — Spend your final afternoon at a smaller, less-crowded gem: the Palazzo Doria Pamphilj (private palace gallery with Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X and Caravaggio works; mid-range ticket) or the MAXXI contemporary art museum. Alternatively, revisit your favorite piazza for a final gelato and people-watching session.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Stroll — End your Roman journey with a meaningful final dinner near your hotel in Borgo or Prati. After dinner, take one last evening walk to St. Peter's Square — illuminated at night, with far fewer crowds than during the day, it's a magical and emotional farewell to Rome.

meals.breakfast: Long, indulgent breakfast at Sciascia Caffè (Via Fabio Massimo, Prati) — Rome's most legendary coffee bar, famous for its thick, velvety espresso and beautiful Art Deco interior. A perfect final morning ritual.
meals.lunch: Mercato Trionfale covered market (Via Andrea Doria, Prati) — Rome's largest and most authentic covered food market, open Sunday mornings. Graze on fresh produce, local cheeses, cured meats, and street food for a true local experience.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Il Sorpasso or book a special final dinner at Osteria dell'Ara Coeli (near Piazza Venezia) — seasonal Roman cuisine in a warm, intimate setting. Order the tiramisu and a digestivo to close out the trip in style.

day_by_day.notes: If departing on June 22, confirm your flight time and arrange airport transport the night before. The Leonardo Express runs from Roma Termini to Fiumicino every 30 minutes; journey takes 32 minutes. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Leave a review for your boutique hotel if you enjoyed the stay!

experiences.description: Walk through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire, exploring the ruins of the Forum where Julius Caesar once stood, and climb Palatine Hill for panoramic views over the city. Combined with the Colosseum ticket, this archaeological site offers an unparalleled journey through 2,000 years of art, architecture, and history.
experiences.location: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum, Ancient Rome district

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transfer — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Private chauffeur transfer from Fiumicino Airport to your boutique hotel in the Borgo district (Vatican City area). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your luxury accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely Neighborhood Orientation Stroll — After settling in, take a relaxed self-guided walk through the charming Borgo district. Explore the iconic Castel Sant'Angelo and stroll along the Lungotevere riverside promenade. Stop at a nearby enoteca for a welcome Aperol Spritz or a glass of local Frascati wine to ease into Roman life.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — Join a premium guided evening food tour through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere. Sample supplì (fried rice balls), Roman-style artichokes, cured meats, aged Pecorino Romano, and pair everything with curated local wines. A perfect sensory introduction to Roman culinary culture.

meals.breakfast: Enjoyed on the flight or at the airport — no hotel breakfast on Day 1.
meals.lunch: Light arrival meal at Il Sorpasso (Prati district, 5 min from hotel) — a stylish Roman bistro offering seasonal cicchetti, charcuterie boards, and natural wines. Perfect post-flight bite.
meals.dinner: Included as part of the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk; conclude the evening with a digestivo at a Trastevere wine bar such as Enoteca Ferrara.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through your hotel concierge. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag management is key for a premium experience. Confirm Trastevere tour booking for evening slot (typically 18:30–21:30).

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel — Begin the day with an exclusive early-access private guided tour of the Vatican Museums, one of the world's greatest art collections. Walk through the Gallery of Maps, the Raphael Rooms, and culminate in a breathtaking, crowd-free experience inside Michelangelo's Sistine Chapel. A skip-the-line premium booking is essential.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Peter's Basilica & Dome Climb — Transition seamlessly from the Museums into St. Peter's Basilica (steps away from your hotel). Admire Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's monumental baldachin. Climb to the top of the dome for sweeping panoramic views over Rome. Afterward, enjoy a relaxed espresso at a café in Piazza del Risorgimento.
day_by_day.evening: Fine Dining in Prati — Unwind with a luxurious dinner at Settimio all'Arancio or the acclaimed Il Matriciano, a historic Roman trattoria beloved by artists and intellectuals, serving classic Roman dishes like cacio e pepe, coda alla vaccinara, and abbacchio al forno.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel — expect a curated spread of cornetti, seasonal fruit, local cheeses, prosciutto, and freshly brewed espresso.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Ristorante Il Sorpasso or Pizzarium Bonci (Prati) — Rome's legendary gourmet pizza al taglio spot, just minutes from the Vatican. Try the potato-rosemary and truffle varieties.
meals.dinner: Il Matriciano (Via dei Gracchi, Prati) — a classic Roman institution. Reserve in advance. Budget approx. €80–120 per person with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican Museums early-access private tour well in advance (3–6 months recommended for June). Dress code for St. Peter's: covered shoulders and knees required. Your hotel concierge can arrange premium skip-the-line access.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour — Take a private chauffeured car to the Villa Borghese park for an exclusive guided tour of the Borghese Gallery. Marvel at Bernini's breathtaking sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic masterworks. Entry is strictly timed and limited — a premium pre-booked private tour elevates this experience significantly.
day_by_day.afternoon: Villa Borghese Gardens & Pincian Hill Terrace — After the gallery, stroll through the manicured Villa Borghese gardens. Rent a rowboat on the ornamental lake or simply relax amid the umbrella pines. Walk to the Pincian Hill terrace (Terrazza del Pincio) for one of Rome's most spectacular panoramic views over Piazza del Popolo and the city skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Pasta & Gelato Making Class — Participate in an intimate hands-on cooking class in a traditional Roman kitchen. A local chef guides you through making fresh pasta (cacio e pepe or carbonara) from scratch, followed by crafting artisanal gelato. Classes typically run 18:00–21:00 and conclude with a convivial dinner of everything you've made, paired with Italian wines.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — request a full Roman breakfast with freshly squeezed blood orange juice and a selection of pastries.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style luxury lunch in Villa Borghese gardens — ask your hotel to prepare or source a premium picnic hamper with local salumi, cheeses, bruschetta, and a chilled bottle of Vermentino.
meals.dinner: Included in the Pasta & Gelato Making Class experience — a full sit-down dinner of your own creations with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery limits visitors to 2-hour timed slots and sells out weeks in advance — book immediately. The gallery is a 15-minute drive from the Borgo district. Cooking class venues vary; confirm location and transport with your hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Exploration — Journey to the ancient heart of Rome with a private expert-guided tour of the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. Walk the Via Sacra where Julius Caesar once tread, explore the Arch of Titus, the Temple of Saturn, and ascend Palatine Hill for sweeping views over the Colosseum and Circus Maximus. A private guide transforms ruins into vivid living history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Colosseum Private Tour & Capitoline Museums — Continue with a premium Colosseum experience including access to the arena floor and underground hypogeum (pre-book exclusive access). Afterward, visit the nearby Capitoline Museums — the world's oldest public museums — to admire the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue and Caravaggio's St. John the Baptist.
day_by_day.evening: Romantic Dinner in the Historic Center — End the day with an exquisite dinner at Ristorante Aroma (rooftop with direct Colosseum views) or La Pergola (Rome's only three-Michelin-star restaurant atop the Rome Cavalieri hotel) for an ultra-premium culinary experience featuring modern Italian haute cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — try the full spread with Roman-style cornetto al pistacchio and a double macchiato.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Ristorante Terre e Domus (near the Forum) — a refined restaurant showcasing Lazio regional cuisine and local wines from the Castelli Romani hills. Try the fettuccine with lamb ragù.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Aroma (Via Labicana) for a stunning rooftop Colosseum view dinner, or La Pergola (Via Cadlolo) for Michelin three-star excellence. Reserve 2–3 months in advance for La Pergola. Budget €150–300+ per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Forum/Palatine/Colosseum complex is approximately 25 minutes by private car from the Borgo district. Book Colosseum underground/arena floor access separately — it sells out quickly. Smart evening attire required for La Pergola.

day_by_day.morning: Piazza Navona, Pantheon & Hidden Baroque Rome — Explore Rome's magnificent Baroque heart with a private art and architecture walking tour. Begin at Piazza Navona to admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, then walk to the awe-inspiring Pantheon (book priority entry). Discover hidden gems: Sant'Ivo alla Sapienza, Palazzo Altemps, and the mysterious Elephant Obelisk in Piazza della Minerva.
day_by_day.afternoon: Campo de' Fiori Market & Artisan Shopping — Stroll through Campo de' Fiori for a taste of local Roman life. Browse artisan food stalls for local honey, truffles, and aged balsamic. Continue to the elegant Via dei Coronari antique street and the luxury boutiques along Via del Babuino. Visit Doria Pamphilj Gallery for a quieter, world-class art experience (Velázquez, Caravaggio, Bernini).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Aperitivo & Rooftop Dining — Enjoy a premium aperitivo hour at the rooftop bar of the Terrazza Borromini (Piazza Navona area) with Negronis and Roman snacks as the sun sets over the city. Follow with dinner at Il Convivio Troiani — a Michelin-starred restaurant in a 15th-century palazzo offering refined modern Roman cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — opt for yogurt with local honey, fresh figs (in season in June), and a brioche.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Osteria dell'Enoteca or Ristorante Fortunato al Pantheon — a Roman institution since 1975, beloved by politicians and artists. Try the rigatoni all'amatriciana and saltimbocca alla romana.
meals.dinner: Il Convivio Troiani (Vicolo dei Soldati) — Michelin-starred, intimate, exceptional tasting menu with Roman ingredients elevated to haute cuisine. Reserve in advance. Budget €120–180 per person with wine pairing.

day_by_day.notes: The Pantheon now requires timed entry tickets — book online. Doria Pamphilj Gallery is often overlooked by tourists but holds extraordinary works. This is a walking-intensive day; wear comfortable but stylish shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Day Trip to Frascati & Castelli Romani Wine Country — Escape the city for a private half-day excursion to the Castelli Romani hills (30 minutes from Rome). Visit a prestigious winery in Frascati for an exclusive cellar tour and tasting of local white wines (Frascati Superiore DOCG). Explore the hilltop town of Frascati with its grand villas and panoramic views back toward Rome.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tivoli & Villa d'Este — Continue to the UNESCO-listed Villa d'Este in Tivoli for an afternoon of Renaissance splendor. Wander through the extraordinary terraced gardens filled with hundreds of fountains, water organs, and cypress-lined allées. Optionally visit the ancient Roman Villa Adriana (Hadrian's Villa) nearby — a vast archaeological complex and UNESCO site.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome — Farewell Gourmet Dinner — Return to Rome by private car in the early evening. Enjoy a leisurely final full-day dinner at Ristorante Glass Hostaria in Trastevere — a chic, design-forward Michelin-starred restaurant offering creative Italian cuisine with an exceptional natural wine list.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure — request a packed espresso thermos and pastries for the road if departing before 8:00.
meals.lunch: Wine and food pairing lunch at the Frascati winery — typically included in premium tour packages. Expect local porchetta, Pecorino, bruschetta al pomodoro, and multiple wine pours.
meals.dinner: Glass Hostaria (Vicolo del Cinque, Trastevere) — Michelin-starred, innovative, beautifully designed. Chef Cristina Bowerman's creative menu is a highlight of Roman fine dining. Budget €100–160 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a private driver for the full day — a luxury car service is recommended for comfort on the Frascati/Tivoli circuit. Pre-book Villa d'Este entry tickets. This is a full and rewarding day — pace yourself.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise at St. Peter's Square & Final Vatican Moments — On your last morning, wake early to experience the magical tranquility of St. Peter's Square at sunrise — virtually empty and extraordinarily beautiful. Attend Sunday Mass or the Papal Angelus blessing (if the Pope is in residence) at noon in the square. Stroll the Borgo district one final time, picking up artisan souvenirs: Roman ceramic tiles, local olive oils, or a bottle of aged Grappa.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury Spa & Leisure — Return to your boutique hotel for a relaxed check-out experience. If your flight allows, indulge in a final Roman spa treatment or a long, slow lunch at a nearby restaurant. Visit the nearby Piazza del Popolo and its twin Baroque churches for one last art moment, or browse the premium food emporium Eataly (Ostiense) for gourmet Italian take-home gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Departure Preparation — Enjoy a final elegant dinner at Osteria dell'Angelo (Prati, near the hotel) — an authentic neighborhood Roman trattoria beloved by locals, serving the five classic Roman pasta dishes and exceptional Roman-Jewish artichoke. Toast to an unforgettable Roman journey with a glass of Barolo. Arrange private chauffeur transfer to the airport for your departure.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — savor it slowly. Request a special spread: freshly baked cornetti, seasonal fruit, local ricotta with honey, and the finest espresso.
meals.lunch: Long Sunday lunch at Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio or Da Enzo al 29 (Trastevere) — a beloved Roman trattoria with market-fresh ingredients and Sunday specials like slow-cooked oxtail and ricotta-filled ravioli.
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo (Via G. Bettolo, Prati) — quintessential Roman trattoria, 5 minutes from your hotel. Reservations essential even on a Sunday. Fixed menu format; extraordinary value for quality. Budget €50–70 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure transfer with hotel concierge the evening before. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for Fiumicino Airport check-in. Pack any wine, olive oil, or food purchases carefully in checked luggage. A 7-day Roman journey like this is best concluded slowly — resist the urge to over-schedule the final morning.
